headline: Showers end tonight; a cold, dry weekend follows, with freezing temperatures and frost early Saturday and mostly dry weather into early next week.
summary: As of Friday evening, leftover showers fade this evening as the upper-level low pressure system that brought them weakens and moves south. The weekend stays dry and cool, with afternoon highs in the low 50s. Trick-or-treaters should have dry weather, but it will be cold. The main concern is early Saturday morning, when skies clear and winds go light. A Freeze Warning (midnight to 9 AM Saturday) covers the lowlands of Lewis and southern Thurston Counties and the Middle Chehalis River Valley, where lows are expected in the upper 20s to low 30s. A Frost Advisory for the same hours covers the northern Olympic Peninsula and areas north of Seattle, including the Eastside, Everett, Marysville, Shoreline, Lynnwood, eastern Kitsap County, and the western Skagit and Whatcom lowlands, with temperatures of 32 to 36 possible. Forecasters advise protecting sensitive plants. Sunday morning will again be near freezing, in the low 30s. A ridge of high pressure (a zone of sinking, stable air) keeps things mostly dry into the first half of next week, though a few weak disturbances could bring light rain chances west of Puget Sound early in the week and around midweek. A stronger front later in the week looks more likely to bring a pattern change, but forecasters say the details are quite uncertain because computer models increasingly disagree. Confidence is high for the dry, cool weekend and cold Saturday start, and reasonably good for mostly dry weather early next week.
changes: The 8:44 PM update added a Frost Advisory for areas north of Seattle and the northern Olympics, and the freeze concern now includes lows in the low 30s Sunday morning. Forecasters also now describe the late-next-week pattern as a more likely change from dry weather, though quite uncertain, instead of a simple Thursday chance of rain.
